newsitem.title: UK: Commodity regulator summit gets underway.
newsitem.headline: Commodity regulator summit gets underway.

text.p: A global meeting between regulators from 18 countries focussing on commodities got underway, as scheduled, earlier on Monday.

Britain's top regulator the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) co-hosts the meeting with the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI).
The day and a half of meetings are addressing the design of commodity futures contracts, surveillance, and, as a consequence, information sharing between regulators, SIB spokesmen said.

The talks are expected to result in a statement of ideals, although the meeting is more a "mapping-out" exercise and sharing of information between regulators, some from emerging countries - who do not normally liase.

Meanwhile, the SIB as well as the American and Japanese regulators and fraud squads is also involved in a global inquiry into events surrounding the dismissal on June 14 of Yasuo Hamanaka, head copper trader for Japan's metals conglomerate Sumitomo Corp.
Sumitomo alleges that Hamanaka was a maverick who ran up losses worth $2.6 billion on unauthorized deals. He was dismissed by Sumitomo in June.
The SIB is carrying out a wide-ranging review of the London Metal Exchange (LME), and will report its findings in December.
And Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) is currently carrying out its own investigation into the copper scandal. "It (the investigation) continues," an SFO spokeswoman said on Monday.
